places.name: Home
places.description: The single most common name experiencers give the place they arrive at is not heaven, the light, or the other side — it is home. They are not describing a beautiful strange country; they are describing arrival at the place they came from and had somehow mislaid. The recognition is instant and total, and it arrives before any being speaks, before any landscape is examined. Many say the word is the only word that fits, and then apologise that it is not enough.

aliases.note: the bare word, used as a proper noun for the destination
the most frequent verbatim formula
used by Eben Alexander and others
one experiencer's intensifier when 'home' proved too weak

places.regex: (?:welcomed? home\b|(?:real|true|eternal|spiritual|actual|forever) home\b|homecoming|(?:felt|feels|feeling|sense|sensation) (?:like |of |that )?(?:i(?:'m| am| was)? )?(?:being )?home\b|knew (?:that )?(?:i was|this was|it was|we were) home\b|(?<!while )i(?:'m| am| was) (?:finally |truly )?home\b(?!\s*[,.]?\s*(?:a few|alone|in bed|in the|with|from|when|for |by myself|sick|recovering|and (?:my|the|we|she|he|i|recovering)))|home at last)
places.negative_regex: while i was home|homeless|nursing home|funeral home|home ?town|home run|welcome home to youtube

quotes.text: I was home. I was home. And I knew it. There's a sense of being home like you will never have here. It was total home. And I didn't want to leave.
the only word I can come up with that is even close to what I felt is, "I was home."
I was home. I felt infinite grace, boundless joy, perfect peace, wholeness, complete acceptance, and total adoration.
But at the same time, it was so familiar to me, as if I had always been there, as if it was my home.
it seemed like a spiritual home. And in many ways, it was far more real than this world.

sensory: an immediate, physical sense of relief — 'you could breathe'
described as bodily, not abstract: one man begins to run on ground he can feel
compared to a dead phone being plugged into its charger
no orientation period; the recognition precedes any inspection of the place
often accompanied by the thought 'I am never leaving'
places.notes: This is the strongest 'return' signal in the corpus and it strengthens monotonically with evidential quality: 14.12% of all accounts, 17.13% at cvNDE>=18, 19.34% at cvNDE>=23. That upward gradient is the opposite of what a culturally-scripted embellishment would do. The word cuts across traditions — Christian, secular, Buddhist and Indigenous experiencers all reach for 'home' unprompted, and several explicitly reject 'heaven' as the wrong word. Precision loss comes from biographical uses ('I was home in bed when I died'), which the lookaheads suppress but do not eliminate.

places.name: Welcome Home
places.description: The greeting itself, reported as a fixed formula: the beings, the crowd, or a single relative say 'welcome home', often adding 'we've been waiting for you'. It is not merely a greeting to a visitor — it is spoken as a return. Experiencers who had no home in life report this as the most emotionally overwhelming moment of the whole experience.

aliases.note: the exact phrase, frequently in quotation marks in the transcript
the usual second clause
spoken by a meditation teacher's presence in one account

places.negative_regex: welcome home to youtube|welcome home from (?:the )?(?:war|deployment|hospital)

quotes.text: Welcome home. Welcome. We've been waiting for you.
my grandfather is extending his hands to me and saying, "Welcome home, Donnie," in a language I've never heard before, but fully understood.
Then I heard her speak inside my mind, "Welcome home. You have come home."
they communicated to me a thought, a meaning, a perception of welcome home. And I'll tell you, it was the most emotional homecoming I think I could have ever experienced
that feeling of being welcomed home was so rich, so real

sensory: arrives telepathically as a whole meaning rather than as words
sometimes spoken in an unknown language that is nevertheless understood
delivered by a crowd speaking as one voice
reported by people who grew up in foster care or dysfunctional homes as unbearable in its sweetness
places.notes: Distinct from the already-catalogued welcoming-party (who is there) — this entry is what is said. Note the drop at cvNDE>=23 (0.55%, 1 of 181): the very best-evidenced accounts are dominated by short, medically-verified OBEs that never reach the greeting stage, so absence here is a truncation artefact, not disconfirmation.

places.name: More Real Than Real
places.description: Experiencers insist, almost defensively, that the other place was not dreamlike but the reverse: more solid, more detailed, more present than waking life. The comparison is volunteered without prompting and is usually offered as the reason they cannot accept a hallucination explanation. The phrasing collapses into a small set of near-identical formulas across thousands of unrelated accounts.

aliases.term: more real than anything I've ever experienced

aliases.note: Eben Alexander's coinage, now widespread

aliases.term: the most real thing that ever happened to me

quotes.text: it felt more real than this life. Yeah. It felt more significant than this life. It felt better in every way than this life.
that was realer than realer than real. And, you know, again, that reminds me just how not real this place is.
This, this place of reality that I was in, this different dimension, was way more real than this place.
more real than anything I'd ever experienced here, and I've concluded that that's my real home.

sensory: detail described as inexhaustible — every blade of grass individually perceived
colour and sound reported as saturated beyond earthly range
memory of it does not fade or blur with decades, unlike ordinary memory
the body on the table becomes 'less interesting', visually thinner than the spiritual form
places.notes: The claim is remarkably stable across strata — 7.48% overall, 8.84% at cvNDE>=18, 9.39% at cvNDE>=23 — i.e. it does not weaken among the accounts with the best-evidenced veridical perception. Frequently co-occurs with the-home in the same sentence; several accounts explicitly link them ('it feels more real, and so that gives you that feeling of being home').

places.name: This Life Is the Dream
places.description: The inversion. Having named the other place the real one, experiencers demote this one: earthly life is the dream, the shadow, the illusion, the murky film. The claim is almost always made after return and in the past tense of comparison — it is the residue of the visit rather than something perceived during it. Several say the demotion never wore off.

aliases.note: the compressed formula
younger experiencers' framing

places.regex: (?:(?:this|the physical|the earthly|earth(?:ly)?) (?:life|world|plane|reality|existence|realm|dimension)[^.!?]{0,30}(?:is|was|seems|seemed|felt like|feels like) (?:more like )?(?:the |a |an )?(?:dream|illusion|hologram|simulation|shadow|not real|unreal|less real)|less real than|this is the dream\b|this life is (?:a |the )?(?:shadow|dream|illusion)|(?:this|here) (?:is|was) (?:the )?(?:fake|illusion))
places.negative_regex: heaven is real|god is real|this is a dream\?|was it a dream

quotes.text: This is the dream. This world, this material world is the murky, kind of dreamlike world.
This life feels like a dream. Feels like I'm walking in a dream because I'm confined in this body with limited mental ability, and I long to go back home
This is the dream. Heaven and all the things that are spiritual is the real thing.
he says that it's like a shadow, this life is a shadow compared to that life.
When you cross over, it's alive. This is like that dream. This is the dream state, sort of like that dream.

sensory: this world described as heavy, slow, 'hip-deep molasses'
emotions here felt as condensed and raging by comparison
the body experienced as a confinement that limits mental bandwidth
places.notes: Deliberately measured separately from more-real-than-real, and it is far rarer (1.30% vs 7.48%). The asymmetry is the finding: many people will say the other place was more real; comparatively few take the further step of calling THIS one a dream. The zero at cvNDE>=23 (0/181) is a small-denominator effect but worth flagging — the strongest veridical cases lean toward sober medical description rather than metaphysical inversion.

places.name: The Recognition — I Had Been Here Before
places.description: The other world is reported not as strange but as remembered. People say it felt familiar, that they recognised the place, that they had been there before — often while simultaneously acknowledging they had never seen it in this life. The familiarity extends to the beings ('I know these people'), the light ('it had always been there and I just forgot'), and the knowledge itself. Several describe the total absence of the astonishment they would have expected.

aliases.note: the most common formula

aliases.term: as if I had always been there

aliases.note: occasionally used as the nearest earthly analogue
the absence of surprise, reported as itself surprising

places.regex: (?:(?:felt|feels|seemed|was|were) (?:so |very |strangely |oddly |completely |totally )?familiar\b(?! with)|sense of familiarity|feeling of familiarity|familiar place|i(?:'d| had) been there before|i(?:'ve| have) been there before|i recogni[sz]ed (?:this place|the place)|i knew (?:this|that) place|knew (?:i|we) (?:had )?been (?:there|here) before)

quotes.text: I recognized this complex, and I knew I'd been there before
It was like, I've been there before. I've done it. I know these people.
I didn't feel surprised to be there, it was something that seems like I had been there before, it was a very natural thing.
it was familiar, like it had always been there and I just forgot about it.
they felt more like family than the people I had seen. And they felt so familiar and so loving.
oh, okay, I recognize this. This feels familiar.

sensory: the strangeness and the familiarity are reported simultaneously and without contradiction
recognition of faces that are not faces from this life
no wonder or tourist astonishment — the tone is 'yeah, okay, expected'
recognition of the darkness as well as the light in some accounts
places.notes: Rises gently with evidential quality (7.14% -> 8.15% -> 8.29%). Precision was measured across two samples: 12/12 clean at cvNDE>=18, roughly 9/14 in the mixed-quality sample, giving ~0.85 overall. The dominant false positive removed by the negative lookahead is 'familiar with' meaning merely acquainted. This is the same underlying report as the-home seen from a different angle — home is what the place IS, recognition is how it is known — and they co-occur heavily.

places.name: Where We Came From
places.description: Beyond familiarity, a stronger claim: this is the place of origin, and the earthly life was the departure from it. Experiencers describe arriving back at a starting point rather than reaching a destination. It is often told as a discovery made in the moment — 'I know that this is where I came from' — and is frequently what converts the experience from an event into a cosmology.

aliases.term: I knew you before you were ever born
aliases.note: scriptural framing offered by Christian experiencers

places.regex: (?:(?:back|return(?:ing)?|go(?:ing)?) (?:to |home to )?where (?:i|we) (?:all )?(?:came|come) from|(?:this|that)(?:'s| is| was) where (?:i|we) (?:all )?(?:came|come) from|where (?:i|we) all (?:came|come) from|(?:i|we) (?:came|come) from (?:there|that place|the light|the source|god)\b|(?:our|my) (?:original|true|real) home)
places.negative_regex: the (?:church|town|city|country|village|state|neighborhood) (?:i|we) came from|asked where (?:i|we) came from

quotes.text: This is where we came from. This is where we're going to return to. And this is really all that matters.
I really felt like I was going home. This is where I came from.
I got to the actual place we would consider heaven or home where we all came from.
that place is what I believe to be my real home. And this is not all that there is.
I had the feeling ... that that place was my true home

sensory: described as a 'larger matrix' one has been separated from
the sense of arriving at a source rather than a destination
often paired with the immediate refusal to leave again
places.notes: Flat across strata (3.93% / 3.87% / 4.42%) — neither strengthened nor weakened by evidential quality. Overlaps the-home heavily by design; kept separate because the claim is different in kind. Home is a felt quality; 'where I came from' is a cosmological assertion about origin, and it is the hinge on which many accounts turn toward pre-birth existence and reincarnation language. False positives are biographical ('the church I came from') and are handled by the negative regex.

places.name: Remembering Who You Really Are
places.description: A specific event inside the experience: an amnesia lifts and the person remembers their own identity — not their biography but what they were before the biography. Several describe it as the veil of forgetting being drawn back, and report astonishment that such a thing could have been forgotten at all. The mirror-image report is equally common: on return, they forget again, and know that they have forgotten.

aliases.note: the inverse, describing incarnation

aliases.term: the veil of forgetting had been lifted
I remembered that I was source
I've known all this, but why did I forget it?

aliases.note: one experiencer's later framing of the same moment

places.regex: (?:remembered who (?:i|we|you) (?:really |truly )?(?:was|am|are|were)|forgot(?:ten)? who (?:i|we|you) (?:really |truly )?(?:was|am|are|were)|remembered (?:my|our) (?:soul|true|real|divine|eternal)|remembered everything (?:about|from) (?:before|my soul)|(?:it|this) (?:was|felt) like (?:i|you|we) (?:had )?always known|(?:i|we) (?:had )?always known (?:this|it|that place)|i (?:just )?forgot\b[^.!?]{0,40}(?:when i (?:came|got) here|born))

quotes.text: I literally remembered who I was. And as if the veil of forgetting had been lifted, and I remembered that I was source.
I remembered why I came here. I remembered who I am. I remembered what's happening.
How could I possibly have forgotten who I really am? How could I have forgotten all these life experiences?
Why did I forget all this?

sensory: reported as a lifting or drawing-back, not as being told
arrives with the memory of choosing this life
the forgetting is described as structural, a condition of being born, not a personal failure
on return the knowledge drains away and the loss is felt as it happens
places.notes: Deliberately narrow. A looser regex catching 'I remembered everything' reaches 8.4% but is dominated by people remembering the accident, so I discarded it. What is left (1.25%) is the soul-identity sense only, and it holds up at cvNDE>=18 (1.24%). This is the recognition of self that parallels the-recognition's recognition of place; it is adjacent to but distinct from the already-catalogued veil-of-forgetting, which names the barrier rather than the moment it lifts.

places.name: Belonging — And Not Belonging Here
places.description: The other side of home: the conviction that one belongs there, coupled — often in the same breath — with the conviction that one does not belong on earth. Experiencers describe earthly life afterwards as an exile, a posting, a charter trip, a deportation. Some report the not-belonging as a lifelong condition that predated the experience and was only explained by it.

aliases.note: the inverse, reported after return

aliases.term: I'm on a charter trip down here

aliases.note: one experiencer's word for embodied life

places.regex: (?:(?:i|we) (?:don't|do not|didn't|never) belong(?:ed)? (?:here|on earth|in this world|in that body)|(?:this|that|here) (?:is|was) where (?:i|we) belong(?:ed)?|sense of belonging|feeling of belonging|i belong(?:ed)? (?:there|to that place)|(?:i|we) belong(?:ed)? there)

quotes.text: I felt that this is my true home and I belonged there. My presence on Earth looked like a deportation to a stranger, an isolated island that was incompatible and unpleasant.
I belonged to that place ... I belonged. I was happy to be there.
I feel that I'm on a charter trip down here and that I belong to the spiritual world.
This is where I belonged. I felt that this was really, um, home to me in many ways.
This time I was coming home. I was homecoming. I was going home, baby. This is where I belong.

sensory: earth afterwards described as an island, a posting, a base camp
the belonging is felt toward beings never met in this life
reported as relief from a lifelong low-grade misfit feeling
places.notes: This is the only entry in my set that DECLINES with evidential quality (3.42% overall -> 2.49% at cvNDE>=18 -> 2.21% at cvNDE>=23). The likely reason is that belonging language is heavily concentrated in long reflective interviews and post-hoc philosophy, which are more common in the lower-cvNDE strata; the strongest veridical accounts are shorter and more event-focused. Worth flagging honestly rather than smoothing over.

places.name: The Homesickness
places.description: The chronic, sometimes lifelong condition that follows the return: not grief for a person but homesickness for a place. Experiencers use the ordinary word for the ordinary feeling and mean it literally. Some report it beginning before they were even back in the body. Several were explicitly warned by beings that remembering would cause it. One child experiencer described it as being dropped at a bus stop by God, who then forgot to come back.

aliases.note: the word used unprompted and literally

aliases.term: I just want to go back there

aliases.note: one experiencer's clinical name for the same state

quotes.text: I call it homesick for heaven. And I felt like God had dropped me off at a bus stop and had forgotten to pick me up.
I don't want to be able to go back. I, I just, I'm already missing it. I'm already homesick.
turned towards the youth who asked me not to remember because the homesickness could have done me harm
I felt homesick, but I didn't really know it at the time. I just knew like, I I want to be there so bad.
I was lonesome. I was lonesome for what was over on the other side.

sensory: described as a bodily ache rather than an emotion
onset sometimes during the experience itself, before return
can persist for decades and is often mistaken by clinicians for depression
temporarily relieved in the company of other experiencers
places.notes: Rises to 1.66% at cvNDE>=18 from 1.33% overall. This is the emotional cost side of the home claim and it is measured with an unusually clean single-word regex — 'homesick' is almost never used biographically in these transcripts. The single cvNDE>=23 hit is a genuine one. Related to but distinct from the catalogued refusal-to-return, which happens at the threshold; this one is the aftermath, and it is what experiencers say ruined or reordered their subsequent lives.

places.name: The Anger and Grief of Coming Back
places.description: The first emotion on regaining the body is very often not gratitude but rage. Experiencers report being furious at the rescuer, the phone call, the paramedic, God, or themselves for the decision to return. Some describe years of clinical depression that they later re-diagnosed as resistance to being back. Small children who could not explain it refused food and refused to be touched.

aliases.term: I was so angry that I came back
why did you bring me back

aliases.note: the diagnosis given to the state
one experiencer's image for re-embodiment

places.regex: (?:(?<!not )(?<!n't )(?:angry|furious|devastated|resentful|bitter|mad)\b[^.!?]{0,70}(?:i (?:was|had to|got) (?:sent |brought )?back|being back|coming back|to (?:come|go) back|(?:they|god|he) sent me back|brought me back|had to return|i (?:came|was) back)|(?:(?:sent|brought) me back|i (?:was|came) back|being back|back in (?:my|this) body)[^.!?]{0,70}(?<!not )(?<!n't )(?:angry|furious|devastated|resentful|bitter|betrayed)\b)

quotes.text: I'm so mad. I was so mad. I, I was so mad that I didn't stay there. I was so mad that I came back here
And I realize now it was because I was so angry and I was resisting being back.
I came back and I was very angry that I was back and wished that this call had not come through and broken up my experience.
now I'm just back in this body, made me feel very, very angry.
I was angry because I'm like, I just want to go back there.

sensory: the anger arrives with the cold and the pain of the returning body
in children: refusal to eat, refusal to be touched, withdrawal
the rescuer or the ringing phone becomes the object of the rage
years-long depression later reinterpreted as unresolved resistance
places.notes: Highest in the best-evidenced stratum (1.66% at cvNDE>=23 vs 1.05% overall), though on small numbers. This entry is measured with a proximity regex requiring the anger and the return to sit in the same clause, because bare anger words appear in 21% of transcripts for unrelated biographical reasons. Distinct from the catalogued heaviness-of-re-entry (the physical weight) and refusal-to-return (the decision at the threshold): this is the emotional aftermath of having lost the place.

places.name: Earth as the Trip, Not the Home
places.description: The framing that makes the home claim coherent: earthly life is temporary and instrumental — a school, a classroom, a base camp, a passage, a trip you took on purpose. Several experiencers report being explicitly corrected on this point by a being: it is a classroom, not a courtroom. The framing is presented as taught information rather than as personal opinion.

aliases.note: recurring near-verbatim formula

aliases.term: life here is just a passage
spiritual beings having a human experience
aliases.note: the most-quoted formula in the corpus

places.regex: (?:spiritual beings having a human experience|(?:earth|this life|this world|this place) is (?:just )?(?:a|like a) (?:school|classroom|schoolhouse|base camp|training ground|university|boot camp|playground|game)|(?:we|i) (?:are|were|'re) (?:just )?(?:here )?(?:on a trip|passing through|on a charter)|school for souls|(?:earth|this life) (?:is|was) (?:just )?(?:a )?temporary)

quotes.text: life on Earth is just a classroom. We come here so we can learn, and that's it.
Earth is just a school. That it's always been just a classroom, and it's never been a courtroom.
life here... is just a passage. We are just passing through, we are pilgrims.
This is temporary. That's all it is.
when we were in our home space, our home space is so permeated with love

sensory: presented as instruction received, often from a named guide
the correction 'classroom not courtroom' delivered as a relief from expected judgement
earth viewed from outside as small, temporary, and purposeful
places.notes: This is the entry that climbs most steeply with evidential quality: 1.13% overall, 2.07% at cvNDE>=18, 2.76% at cvNDE>=23 — more than doubling. It is the cosmological complement to the-home: if that place is home, this one has to be explained, and the corpus's own explanation is school, passage, or trip. Note that the 'classroom not courtroom' phrasing clusters in accounts connected to one experiencer (Vincent/Vinney Tolman) appearing under multiple video ids, so the true independent-witness count is lower than the document count suggests.
